correctness.rationale: The printed reset gives \(x(0)=(1-p)h\), \(x(T^-)=h\), and \(y(0)=(1-q)y(T^-)+\tau>\tau\). Dividing the prey equation by \(x>0\) proves the exact logarithmic budget. From \(\dot y\ge-\beta y\), one obtains \(y(t)>\tau e^{-\beta t}\); first-return geometry gives \(x(t)<h\). These inequalities yield the displayed integral correction exactly. The derivative \(F'(T)=\rho-\lambda\tau e^{-\beta T}/(h+\tau e^{-\beta T})\) is positive for \(T>0\) under the stated condition, giving a unique root. The packaged computation checks both numerical roots; no finite experiment substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly treats the order-one period as a management quantity and optimizes an economic objective divided by period. The release-corrected bound uses compulsory predator stocking and natural predator decay to constrain feasible intervention frequency without trajectory integration. At the source example it raises the necessary floor from \(1.5541\ldots\) to \(2.3686\ldots\), and at the reported optimum from \(0.4727\ldots\) to \(0.6782\ldots\), a substantive improvement tied directly to the model's control mechanism.
